hints: Differentiate both parametric equations with respect to $t$.
Use $dy/dx=(dy/dt)/(dx/dt)$ with $dx/dt=2t$ and differentiate $\ln(2t-1)$ by the chain rule.
Combine the result into the requested rational expression in $t$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the parametric equation for $x$, $x = t^2 + 1$, with respect to $t$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t^2 + 1) = 2t$$

Differentiate the parametric equation for $y$, $y = 4t + \ln(2t - 1)$, with respect to $t$ using the chain rule on $\ln(2t - 1)$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = 4 + \dfrac{1}{2t - 1} \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2t - 1) = 4 + \dfrac{2}{2t - 1}$$

Combine the terms of $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}$ over a common denominator:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{4(2t - 1) + 2}{2t - 1} = \dfrac{8t - 4 + 2}{2t - 1} = \dfrac{8t - 2}{2t - 1}$$

Apply the chain rule formula for parametric differentiation, $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y/\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}x/\mathrm{d}t}$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\dfrac{8t - 2}{2t - 1}}{2t} = \dfrac{8t - 2}{2t(2t - 1)}$$
(Or equivalently: $\dfrac{4t - 1}{t(2t - 1)} = \dfrac{2}{t} + \dfrac{2}{4t^2 - 2t}$).

ai_rubric.Differentiating Parametric Curves: Identifies $\frac{dy}{dt}=4+\frac2{2t-1}$; Applies $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dy}{dt}\div\frac{dx}{dt}$; Gives $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{8t-2}{2t(2t-1)}$, or equivalent, e.g. $\frac2t+\frac2{4t^2-2t}$.

hints: Substitute $t=1$ into the parametric equations to find the point and into part (i) to find the tangent gradient.
Take the negative reciprocal for the normal gradient, form its point-gradient equation, and rearrange to $ax+by+c=0$.
walkthrough:
Find the coordinates $(x_1, y_1)$ of the point on the curve corresponding to $t = 1$:
$$x_1 = 1^2 + 1 = 1 + 1 = 2$$
$$y_1 = 4(1) + \ln(2(1) - 1) = 4 + \ln(1) = 4 + 0 = 4$$
So the point on the curve is $(2, 4)$.

Evaluate the gradient of the tangent at $t = 1$ using $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ from part (i):
$$m_{\text{tangent}} = \dfrac{8(1) - 2}{2(1)(2(1) - 1)} = \dfrac{6}{2(1)} = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3$$

Find the gradient of the normal $m_{\text{normal}}$:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\dfrac{1}{m_{\text{tangent}}} = -\dfrac{1}{3}$$

Use the point-slope form of the equation of a straight line, $y - y_1 = m_{\text{normal}}(x - x_1)$:
$$y - 4 = -\dfrac{1}{3}(x - 2)$$

Clear fractions and rearrange terms into the form $ax + by + c = 0$:
$$3(y - 4) = -(x - 2)$$
$$3y - 12 = -x + 2$$
$$x + 3y - 12 - 2 = 0$$
$$x + 3y - 14 = 0$$

ai_rubric.Finding Equations of Normals: Substitution of $t=1$ into $dy/dx=(8t-2)/(2t(2t-1))$ gives tangent gradient $3$ and normal gradient $-1/3$; through $(2,4)$ this gives $x+3y-14=0$.
